title.purpose: Section/panel titles — the Mission Hero's objective line, modal titles.

icon.purpose: Rail-style plain-glyph icons (activity bar) — sized for click comfort, not a text role.

body.purpose: The base UI size — buttons, form fields, primary labels.

body-sm.purpose: Secondary body text — list-row detail, section descriptions.

label.purpose: Section kickers and status-row labels, uppercase.

meta.purpose: The smallest text — timestamps, chip labels, fine print.

mono.purpose: File paths, code, terminal output, timestamps, technical/literal values.

shadows.name: ambient-card
shadows.purpose: Barely-there depth for elements that sit slightly above their row (artifact cards).

shadows.name: floating-panel
shadows.purpose: The Mission Hero and similar elevated-but-inline elements.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition easing across hover/focus/collapse states.

motion.name: duration-entrance
motion.purpose: Entrance fades/slides for newly-arrived content (messages, timeline rows, modals) — must respect prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled/high-emphasis button style — used sparingly, one per view where possible.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #3b82f6; color: #e6e9ef; border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2563eb; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button — bordered, transparent background, used for nearly everything else.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #8b93a3; border: 1px solid #2a2f3a; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #1e222b; color: #e6e9ef; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Chip — Go
components.description: Low-opacity tint background, full-opacity status text — the pattern every status chip in the app follows.
components.css: .ds-chip-go { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; background: rgba(34,197,94,0.16); color: #86efac; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; padding: 1px 9px; border-radius: 999px; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Status Chip — Abort
components.description: The failure/danger variant of the same chip pattern.
components.css: .ds-chip-abort { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; background: rgba(239,68,68,0.18); color: #fca5a5; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; padding: 1px 9px; border-radius: 999px; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The base container — flat, bordered, 8px radius. Add ambient-card shadow only when the card should feel lifted.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #171a21; border: 1px solid #2a2f3a; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; } .ds-card:hover { background: #1e222b; } .ds-card-title { font-family: ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 11px; color: #e6e9ef; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 11px; color: #8b93a3; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Text input — console-panel background, hairline border, telemetry-blue focus border with no glow.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #171a21; color: #e6e9ef; border: 1px solid #2a2f3a; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 10px; font-size: 13px; font-family: inherit; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #3b82f6; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #8b93a3; }

components.name: Nav Tab (active)
components.description: The shared toggled/active-state treatment used across the topbar, activity bar, and every internal tab strip.
components.css: .ds-tab { background: transparent; color: #8b93a3; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; padding: 5px 12px; font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab-active { background: rgba(59,130,246,0.15); color: #93c5fd; border-color: rgba(59,130,246,0.4); }

narrative.overview: ATOMIC Studio reads as a cockpit, not a canvas: a dark instrument panel where every signal is real, every status has an honest color, and nothing moves or flashes without a reason. The system is built for two crews at once — a non-coder pilot who needs the console to never lie to them, and a professional engineer who needs it to be fast and dense when they want it to be. Both get the same panel; density and jargon flex, honesty and calm never do. This isn't decorative sci-fi chrome. "Mission Control" is a discipline: status colors mean exactly one thing each (green is genuinely safe, red is genuinely wrong, amber is genuinely a warning — never used for emphasis or decoration), motion is reserved for things that are actually changing, and the interface holds still between changes instead of rearranging itself for novelty's sake.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, low-chroma base with exactly one accent hue (telemetry blue) — color is a signal, not decoration
Flat at rest; shadows appear only on things that are genuinely floating above the base layer
Plain system fonts and plain emoji/unicode glyphs — no icon font, no illustration system
Status semantics borrowed from real instrumentation: go/no-go green and red, caution amber, never repurposed

rules.name: The Go/No-Go Rule
rules.body: go-green, abort-red, and caution-amber mean exactly one thing each — success/safe, failure/dangerous, needs-attention — everywhere in the app, with no exceptions for emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The No-Decoration Type Rule
rules.body: Weight and the uppercase-kicker treatment carry hierarchy — never font-family switching, never italics, never a display face.

rules.name: The Altitude Rule
rules.body: Shadow size is a direct, honest signal of how far above the base plane something sits — never applied for decoration, and never on anything that's actually flat/in-flow.

dos: Do reserve go-green/abort-red/caution-amber for literal status only
Do keep every card and panel bordered in hairline-steel, with or without a shadow
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion for every looping/infinite animation
Do make every interactive element keyboard-operable with a real <button>/aria-expanded
Do let motion mean something — always reporting a real state change
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color
Don't use drop shadows on anything that's actually flat/in-flow
Don't add an icon font, SVG icon library, or illustration system
Don't show a UI element that claims something the app can't back up
